groups.name: Impact of Collective Trauma on Organizational Health
groups.facilitator: Virginia Klamon; Michael Stone; Kathi Buchanan
groups.description:
How Unseen Wounds Shape Culture, Leadership, and Performance
Collective trauma quietly shapes organizational life through burnout, disconnection, toxic culture, low engagement, and resistance to change. Unhealed individual, ancestral, and systemic wounds fuel reactivity, power imbalances, and the erosion of trust and psychological safety. Trauma-informed organizations transform these patterns through nervous-system regulation, deep listening, transparent communication, and relational leadership—restoring trust, inclusion, creativity, resilience, and sustainable human-centered success.

groups.name: Kollektives und Transgenerationales Trauma unserer Beziehungsarchitektur
groups.facilitator: Susanne Breit; Brigitte Kotzke; Daphne Leinweber; Peter Hellwig
groups.description:
Ein gemeinsamer Prozess zur Bewusstwerdung und Transformation von Beziehung
++Die Bewerbung für dieses Lab ist nur noch für Männer geöffnet, um das Geschlechterverhältnis in der Gruppe auszugleichen.++ Wir wenden uns dem kollektiven Erbe zu, das unser weibliches und männliches Sein seit Generationen prägt. Männer und Frauen bringen unterschiedliche soziale und familiäre Muster aus Kollektiv und Ahnenreihe mit, die im Kontakt sichtbar werden. Im Lab schaffen wir ein kohärentes Feld gemeinsamer Ressourcen, synchronisieren Körper und Emotionen und erkunden individuelle wie kollektive Traumata. Im Erforschen der Traumalandschaft kann Verdrängtes auftauchen und bezeugt werden. Durch Einstimmung, Austausch und Reflexion entsteht Integration und Transformation.

groups.name: Trennung von Spiritualität & Körper in Deutschland heilen
groups.description:
Eine Reise durch gesunde und energetische Grenzen
In diesem Lab widmen wir uns den Auswirkungen der deutschen Geschichte auf die Verkörperung von Spiritualität, gesunden, energet. Grenzen und einem Gefühl von Zugehörigkeit. Viele von uns fühlen sich nicht vollständig zuhause im eigenen Körper, nehmen ihn kaum oder als etwas wahr, das es zu überwinden oder zu verbessern gilt.Wir schaffen Raum, unsere Körperweisheit tiefer zu erforschen, persönliche Grenzen und kollektive Muster zu erkennen, um sie zu ehren und beobachten zu können, was bereit ist, sich zu öffnen und zu wandeln in gesunde Grenzen und eine Kraft, die neu ausdrückt, wer wir wirklich sind.

groups.name: Restory-ing Wholeness through the Sacred Feminine
groups.facilitator: Jennifer Edson; Laura Northrop; Holly Gayley
groups.description:
Healing the Wounds of Patriarchy and the Fragmented Self
How do patriarchal wounds live in the female body? Due to gender conditioning, what parts of ourselves have we had to split off and exile to fit into social roles and find belonging? This lab is a nine-month gestation to heal the fragmented self and re-story the sacred feminine into our lives, coming home to a natural sense of authenticity and wholeness. Using the wisdom of nature as our guide, we will flow through seasonal and developmental cycles to integrate the shadow and wounded parts of ourselves into a fresh narrative of possibility. Together, let’s rewild the soul.

groups.name: EarthBound: Collective Trauma Lodged in Place
groups.facilitator: Deep Land; Sarah Rocha, LPC, CCTP, SEP; Amy Ode'imin Lortie, LMT, SEP
groups.description:
As Heart-Wisdom of Land, Alchemizing Embedded Trauma Imprints
Anchored in deep, generous Land, this lab invites us to sit with the collective trauma (CT) embedded in place— the unresolved fragments lingering from conflict, violence, and disasters. These imprints can create injurious patterns that echo the very hurts that they are the remnants of, shaping what comes after. Not limited to humanity, these imprints include the Land itself and all beings with whom we dwell. With humility, we “listen without the expectation of being told.” We remember as Land, meeting and embodying these fragments with presence, respect, and care.

groups.name: From Polarization to Sacred Polarities: Healing the Masculine and Feminine
groups.facilitator: Krista Bremer; Karl Steyaert; Lee Morgan
groups.description:
Women and Men Healing Gender-related Trauma Together.
Please note: To encourage a balance of men and women in this lab, we are now only accepting applications from men. We will explore masculine/feminine polarization and the individual, ancestral, and collective gender wounds that live in our bodies, psyches, relationships, and systems across cultures. We will explore how these wounds manifest in our individual and collective lives — from the most intimate spaces of self and sexuality to the vast arenas of public discourse, political ideologies, and institutional structures. We aim to bring curiosity and awareness to symptoms which include compromised attunement to self and other; distortion of authenticity; and diminished capacities.

groups.name: Nuestros Cuerpos, Nuestro Planeta, Nuestra Separación
groups.facilitator: Catalina Gallo Pelaez; María Emilia Larraondo Franco; Laura Pallares; Marina Vinitsky
groups.description:
Desconexión e inteligencia orgánica de nuestros cuerpos y nuestro planeta
Sentirnos “separados de nuestros cuerpos y de nuestra tierra” es un síntoma del trauma colectivo que vivimos. Durante miles de años nuestros sistemas nerviosos desarrollaron patrones de protección para sobrevivir. En este LAB intencionamos reconocer estos patrones para completar ciclos interrumpidos y restaurar el movimiento orgánico de la vida. Este espacio no busca respuestas intelectuales, sino presencia compartida, escucha sensible y movimiento consciente que habilite reestablecer la confianza en la inteligencia regenerativa de la naturaleza.

groups.name: Othering & the U.S. Political Divide
groups.facilitator: Robert Buxbaum; Bill McCart; Jennifer Krier
groups.description:
Unearthing and Healing the Dynamics that Fragment Us
We all “other” in our personal lives in small and large ways, instantly making someone “bad” for something they do that causes us discomfort. Collectively, the dehumanizing of othering justifies war, genocide, discrimination and subjugation. Why does this reflexive behavior remain unconscious and pervasive despite the conflict and suffering it produces? This lab is an invitation to unpack the process of othering personally and collectively, and rather than othering it, welcome it as a once-important protective mechanism that can transform into an evolutionary invitation to healing discourse.

groups.name: Remembering European Indigeneity in North America Lab
groups.description:
Restoring our Connection with the Forgotten Ancestors of indigenous Europe
European immigrants to North America descended from indigenous ancestors. What happened to the diverse peoples of pre-Christian Europe, and their ancient ways of knowing and being? From the Roman Empire's slaughter and enslavement of indigenous peoples through the Christian persecution of Pagans and beyond, centuries of trauma scar people of European descent in invisible ways. The pain of these wounds positioned Europeans to replicate the same brutality in colonizing the New World. When we reintegrate our ancient European ancestors, we can face present and future from a more resourced place.

groups.name: Relating to Land and Nature
groups.facilitator: Cristina Orbe; Monica Weber; Sue Gallagher
groups.description:
Collective Wounds of Ownership
Through a deeper sensing of how wild and ownership/property live in each of us, our intention is to support the surfacing and integration of disconnection, numbing, fear, perpetration, and victim layers that inform decision-making, habits, attitudes, and behaviors regarding wild land, animals and plants. By attuning to our individual, ancestral, and collective field, we will investigate what arises and what are possible futures and alternatives for relating to wild land, plants and animals including reciprocity, stewardship, and communion.

groups.name: Indian and Residential Boarding Schools
groups.facilitator: Woman Stands Shining - Pat McCabe; Katherine Elizabeth Poco-Enders; Roland Guenther; Kelly Ann Chambers
groups.description:
A Survivor and Descendant Space for Healing and Connection
This Lab centers the lived legacy of Native American boarding and residential schools across North America, where children were taken from their families, languages, and ways of life. The harm did not end with the closure of the schools; it continues through descendants, families, and communities today. Together we will tend grief, resilience, and memory, honoring Survivors and all who carry this history in their bodies, relationships, and lives.Full scholarships are available to participants in this lab. After acceptance, participants will receive a scholarship code to complete registration.

groups.name: The Collective Curse of “Success-ism”
groups.facilitator: Vania Perez Moreno; Prashant Goel; Angela Zinser
groups.description:
Restoring Wholeness Beyond Scarcity and Conditional Worth
Many of us inherit an invisible curse from predominant systems and culture: be extraordinary, be productive, be more. Shaped by colonial legacies, economic structures, and family survival strategies, this conditioning teaches that worth must be earned and belonging is conditional. Over time, it forms “successism”—a collective illness that constricts our agency, burdens us with chronic efforting, and imprints the nervous system toward vigilance and survival. This Lab explores how scarcity and separation live in our bodies, nourishing our capacity to be in service of Life.

groups.name: South Asians: Decolonizing a History of Subjugation
groups.facilitator: Ruchi Puri; Monica Murarka; Our Heritage; Our work with Thomas
groups.description:
Healing Foreign Legacies on South Asian Identity, Heritage & Home Today
We’ll explore how centuries of empire—especially British rule and its exit—sheared the interwoven cultural fabric of South Asian communities, reshaping identities, power and relationship to the subcontinent’s rich spiritual tradition. Generations endured subjugation, partitions, displacement, scarcity, and violence with little space to grieve what was lost or re-connect to ancestral practices. Today, these imprints live on in us. This lab invites us to notice how these collective wounds shape our sense of home, self, belonging, and connection to our roots today.

groups.name: Healing Collective Grief Suppression
groups.facilitator: Suresh Schlanger; Marna Chester; Markus Bomm
groups.description:
Identifying and Befriending Overwhelm, Loneliness and Anxiety in Modernity
This lab is designed to create a collective space to identify and process the cumulative effects and suppressed grief caused by modern day life. We will share in witnessing its impacts, especially those prioritizing efficiency, productivity, competition and domination at the expense of human and ecological well being, and social connection.Through communal witnessing we seek to metabolize the frozen energies into a fluid and vibrant resource for the individual and collective.

groups.name: Unleashing the Suppressed Voice of the Feminine
groups.description:
Expressing Desires, Needs, and Boundaries in Female bodies
This lab is an embodied exploration of voice, desire, and boundaries. We will grow our awareness of how ancestral patterns, family dynamics, cultural expectations, and societal pressures have influenced our relationship to desire and authentic expression. We will uncover and liberate patterns of appeasing, shrinking, numbing, avoiding conflict or suppressing our needs - and how that distorts or silences our voice. Together, we will investigate how our ability to ask for what we want, set clear limits, and speak from the truth of our bodies has been has been shaped by gender conditioning.For this lab, there will be an additional cost—with a suggested donation of $200—to cover the cost of the venue. This will be collected in person at the retreat.

groups.name: The Living Legacy of Dictatorship
groups.facilitator: Dasha Gaian; Lori Amy; Daria Yemets
groups.description:
Digesting the Shadow of Soviet Trauma and its Global Repercussions
This lab explores the trauma of 20th-century authoritarianism. Using the Soviet legacy of colonization, repression, and forced assimilation as a starting point, we investigate dictatorship as an historical system, how the trauma of dictatorship is transmitted across generations and societies, and how these imprints and traumas continue in the 21st century. We also look for the unresolved collective traumas that lead to authoritarianism as well as shared patterns of dictatorship across times and places, with a special emphasis on the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe.

groups.name: Iluminando el Trauma Colectivo de la Maternidad
groups.facilitator: Stephanie Pizarro; Maria Soledad Troya; Veronica Molina Gerstner
groups.description:
Un lab de apoyo, autenticidad y transformación para madres latinoamericanas
La maternidad no solo refleja nuestra historia personal, sino también el peso de experiencias colectivas y ancestrales. Este laboratorio es un viaje compartido de autodescubrimiento, donde exploramos fragmentaciones y desconexiones que habitan en nuestros sistemas familiares y culturales. Es un espacio para sostenernos, sentirnos vistas, sanar y presenciar nuestro camino con mayor conciencia, intuición y amor propio.

groups.name: The Interrupted Conversation with Earth – Global
groups.facilitator: Sally Bell-Cross; Christine Hoenig-Ohnsorg; Liliane Mavridara
groups.description:
The Trauma of Forced Forgetting and the Pathway to Sacred Renewal
Colonization and industrialization persecuted land-based knowledge keepers, severing sacred ties with Earth. Desacralization - the violent stripping of Earth’s sacred aliveness - created a collective trauma of forced forgetting.
We inherited this trauma as ecological amnesia: treating the sacred as expendable, feeling separate from Earth’s community of beings, and losing languages that honored rivers and forests as sacred relatives rather than resources. This trauma shows up today as degraded ecosystems, extractive decision-making, and an inner sense of loneliness and disconnect.

groups.name: Israel: Grief and Transgenerational Trauma
groups.facilitator: Idit Rose; Hagit Ottens-Wilk; Sylvia Silberg
groups.description:
From Collective Wounding to Healing, Integration, and Communal Resilience
In this lab, we will gather to share and bear witness to our collective grief and pain as they surface in the heart of an ongoing war. Through the lens of grief, we will invite awareness to how tension and fragmentation live within and around us, in our bodies, relationships, communities, and social structures. While Israeli society holds many lived realities, this lab focuses on the Jewish-Israeli experience, including intergenerational trauma within the Jewish story, and how it continues to shape the visible and invisible architecture of our lives today.

groups.name: Was bedeutet es, Deutsch zu sein
groups.facilitator: Ingrid Pickel; Bjoern Lasse Herrmann; Britta Möckelmann
groups.description:
Im Spannungsfeld zwischen Gestaltungskraft und deutschem Schatten?
Was hält uns zurück, die Herausforderungen unserer Zeit mutig und kreativ mitzugestalten? Oft scheint ein Nebel aus Angst, Scham und Unsicherheit unser Handeln zu trüben. Die Narben der Vergangenheit erschweren es, im eigenen Deutschsein zu stehen und unserer Vielfalt, Lebendigkeit und Innovationskraft Raum zu geben. In diesem Lab wenden wir uns gemeinsam unseren lebendigen wie verletzten Wurzeln zu, um neue Handlungsfähigkeit, Verbundenheit und Kraft zu entfalten.

groups.name: Der Tod und Wir – Das Stille Tabu
groups.facilitator: Bettina Hallifax; Elke Pfister; Kaja Novak
groups.description:
Kulturelle Verdrängung und die befreiende Kraft der Auseinandersetzung
Tod und Sterben gehören zum Leben – doch wo kollektive Erfahrungen von Krieg, Flucht, plötzlichem Verlust oder verdrängter Trauer wirken, wird Endlichkeit zum Tabu. Diese transgenerationalen Prägungen beeinflussen, wie wir auf Abschied, Wandel und Krise reagieren–oft ohne dass wir es bewusst erkennen. Unser LAB lädt ein, diese unsichtbaren Muster zu erforschen: wie prägen familiäre und kollektive Traumata unser Verhältnis zu Leben und Tod? Ziel ist es, persönliche Ängste und kollektive Schatten zu reflektieren, um Endlichkeit nicht als Bedrohung, sondern als Quelle von Lebendigkeit zu erfahren.

groups.name: Das Dilemma der Schweiz während dem Zweiten Weltkrieg
groups.facilitator: Christoph Häusler; Francois Michael Wiesmann; Liselotte Wyssbrod Ammon
groups.description:
Erforschen der kollektiven Überlebensstrukturen und was darunter liegt.
Nach dem schnellen Sieg Deutschlands über Frankreich 1940 war die Schweiz vollständig von NS-Deutschland und dem faschistischen Italien umgeben. Sie suchte ihre Unversehrtheit und Neutralität durch Diplomatie, wirtschaftliche Kooperation und militärische Bereitschaft zu sichern. Allerdings blieb sie von deutschen Rohstoffen abhängig und unter politischem Druck. Sie bot humanitäre Hilfe, wies aber auch Flüchtlinge ab, auch jüdische. Schweizer Banken profitierten von Raubgold und der Handel mit dem NS-Regime stärkte dessen Kriegsführung. In einigen Kreisen gab es grosse Sympathien für NS-Ideen.

groups.name: Witch Hunts
groups.facilitator: Andrea Livingston; Lysan Boshuyzen; Anne Huhn
groups.description:
Echoes of Europe’s Witch Trials in our Bodies, Lineages and Culture
In this lab, we look closely at witch hunts in Early Modern Europe, which led to 40,000–60,000 (est.) executions, 80% of whom were women. Through this lens, we will explore the role and interplay of religion, colonialism, hysteria, misogyny, and the erasure of Indigenous European spiritual and earth-based practices. How does the generational fear of "being burned at the stake" live on in the archaeology of our bodies and structure society today? Together we will sense how the residues inform our bodies, lineages, and culture, and gently open pathways for integration and collective healing.

groups.name: Argentina: Sintiendo nuestras raíces a través de capas del Trauma Colectivo
groups.description:
El poder del contacto con la tierra interna. Recursos del enraizamiento.
Nuestra energía vital está ligada a lo que puede percibirse como campos de trauma colectivo. Matrices de energía que retienen el dolor del pasado. La energía que alimenta la exclusión, la escasez, la polarización, las repeticiones, está congelada en estos campos, y en nosotros.
La verdadera naturaleza de esta energía, una vez descongelada, es la creatividad, la innovación, la fluidez de recursos.
En Argentina, casi toda la población tiene ancestros inmigrantes. Exploraremos procesos de la colonización agrícola y la vida de los inmigrantes para integrar ese potencial congelado.

groups.name: Deutschland – Russland: Kollektive Wunden
groups.facilitator: Ingolf Hoven; Julia Tzotchev; Marc Leistner
groups.description:
Wie leben diese Wunden in mir und in der deutschen Gesellschaft als Ganzes?
Russland ist ein großes Land, dessen Einfluss in Deutschland und Europa in der einen oder anderen Form immer spürbar ist. Wir erforschen deutsche Identität in Bezug zu Russland, d.h. deutsche Selbstwahrnehmung, Selbstreflexion und ggf. Neuorientierung. Dabei richten wir den Blick auf Themen, die oft im Hintergrund wirken: Schichten historischer Traumata, Ost-West-Spaltung in Deutschland, Fremdheitserfahrungen und Zukunftsängste. Kollektive Wunden bei anderen Völkern durch Deutschland, die Sowjetunion oder Russland werden ausdrücklich anerkannt, sind aber nicht der primäre Fokus dieses Labs.

groups.name: Women Healing from Collective Gender Wounds
groups.description:
Integrating Sacred Female Rage and Exiled Energy into Right Relation
Collective trauma, born from the wounds of gender violence, deeply and powerfully shapes how we relate to ourselves and to one another. It influences our identities, our sense of safety, and our ability to speak and embody our truth. In this lab we are creating and nurturing a space for women to reclaim earth wisdom, ancestral memory, and the vital life force of our sacred female rage—a pathway to embodying our wholeness, reclaiming our voice, and restoring right relational stance with each other and with all beings.

groups.name: Being British: Colonised and Colonisers
groups.description:
Exploring our Roots, Conditioning, and Potential as Catalysts for Healing
This Lab will explore the layered nature of being British — both the ancestral and collective wounds we carry, and the impact these wounds have had on the rest of the world. How does the hierarchical conditioning that sustained the British Empire both at home and abroad live on in us today? What does it mean to carry legacies of perpetration from crimes committed in former colonies? And what would it mean to collectively heal? We intend to discover together the resources that can support the evolution of a new form of British identity, aligned with a more authentic, inclusive future.

groups.name: Collective Stigmatizing of Queer Men – Global
groups.facilitator: Gary Raucher; Brandt Miller; Andres Quezada
groups.description:
Healing the Social and Spiritual Exiling of Non-Heteronormative Men
Modern Western cultures are burdened by a long history in which queer folks are othered, pathologized, and persecuted by religious, social, and political systems. This lab addresses traumas-of-stigmatization that gay/queer and bisexual men of all ethnicities and ages experience as an othered group in many cultures. Honoring both our sensitivity and susceptibility to shame, we will explore our inner strengths, beauty, and deep capacity for self/other intimacy. In maturing our relationships with ourselves and one another, we foster enhanced agency to heal trauma as individuals and community.

groups.name: German Colonial Shadows – Perpetrator Lineages
groups.description:
Presencing German Perpetrator Legacy in Descendants
Collective healing grows when descendants of perpetrators feel supported in facing their own ancestral histories. Germany carries a complex legacy of perpetration - from the Holocaust and WWII to its often-unseen role as the world’s third-largest colonial power. This lab warmly invites participants to explore their relationship to German colonial perpetratorship. As xenophobia and ideas of cultural superiority rise globally, we look to their colonial roots. The lab offers a supportive space for those with perpetrator lineage to soften “colonial amnesia” and reconnect with ancestral history.

groups.name: Journeying with Breast Cancer
groups.facilitator: Teddy Frank; Dana Revnic; Ntombiyethu Biyase
groups.description:
A Path of Personal and Collective Learning and Growth
Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer worldwide (World Health Organization).
What are the personal and collective aspects of trauma for women diagnosed with breast cancer?
Shock, fear of dying, anxiety of a recurrence, grief for loss of fertility, disfigurement, shame, stigma.
Cultural norms of feminine beauty damage women’s self-esteem and body image. Over giving as caretakers, lack of self-care, isolation, all play a role in dis-ease.
The aim in our Lab is to create new architectures of emotional, energetic, ancestral and collective support for women dealing with breast cancer.

groups.name: The Money Lab
groups.facilitator: Melissa Schenker; Ravya Taghavi; Jürgen Wölfl
groups.description:
Exploring how Collective Trauma shows up in our Relationship to Money
The US economic system has a particular ‘flavor’ arising from its unique backstory. This flavor of capitalism, both in the US and beyond, lives in us in unique ways. How we interact with money can illuminate how the system lives in us. Our inner world shapes the systems we create and those systems in turn shape our inner world. We offer a lab to explore the conscious and unconscious material that manifests in our relationship to money. Through embodied inquiry and reflection, we’ll surface awareness of how collective trauma shows up in us.

groups.name: Kollektives Trauma in Bildung und Erziehung
groups.facilitator: Silke Weiß; Adelheid Köhn; Julia Friedel
groups.description:
Die DNA unseres Lernens und Aufwachsens erkennen und transformieren
Wir wollen erforschen, wie kollektives Trauma die Art und Weise wie wir Kinder erziehen und bilden beeinflusst - zu Hause und in Schulen Wir betrachten die Entstehung dieser Systeme im deutschsprachigen Raum, die Einflüsse der deutschen Geschichte darauf und welche Konflikte sich daraus heute in Schule zeigen. Ebenso erforschen wir, welche Erfahrungen uns selbst geprägt haben und wie sie über Generationen weitergegeben werden. Wir fragen, wie eine Umgebung entstehen kann, in der Kinder sich wirklich entfalten können. Im Lauf des Labs integrieren wir die Themen, die Teilnehmende mitbringen.

groups.name: Family Estrangement as a Collective Trauma Pattern
groups.facilitator: Karen Forsthoff; Steven Shumborski; Lee Lahoud
groups.description:
Exploring Landscapes and Pathways of Estrangement and Reconciliation
Family Estrangement is an ambiguous loss where someone we love is physically alive but relationally absent. This gray zone grief often goes unrecognized in our culture. Millions of people across the globe suffer this type of isolating relational trauma. Most estrangements arise through a combination of temperament, social influences, developmental traumas, and the collision of narratives about the past. This type of trauma requires relational healing within an ecosystem of validation and support. Together we will explore the pathways of estrangement and reconciliation as change is possible.

groups.name: Habitando el Cuerpo Latinoamericano
groups.facilitator: Stephanie Pizarro; Maria Soledad Troya; Karla Mejia
groups.description:
Presenciamos la fragmentación interna y colectiva de nuestra América Latina
Si has sentido dolor por tu territorio y te abruma o te conmueve la fragmentación, la violencia, la polarización y las heridas heredadas que cargamos en Latinoamérica, este Laboratorio te invita a crear espacio para exhalar el estrés crónico, explorar con cuidado lo que duele y reconectar con lo vivo en ti y en lo colectivo. Buscamos integrar, desde nuestro cuerpo, comportamientos colectivos que hemos normalizado y que generan miedo, desconfianza, escasez e insensibilidad.

groups.name: Integrating Echoes of Child Abuse in Society
groups.description:
Breaking the Cycles of Abuse: Digesting Echoes of our Childhood together
The echoes of emotional, physical or sexual abuse in our childhood linger within us. 1 in 6 children grow up with some form of abuse from their caregivers. Parents often repeat what they lived as children, forming a cycle of broken attachment and childhood trauma. Survivors may struggle in life in multiple ways, perpetuate emotional abuse, neglect and violence against themselves or others, and cause further harm when in a position of power. Our lab is a safe space to metabolize these wounds so the cycles of harm and suffering do not repeat – in our bodies, relationships, families, and society.

groups.name: El Dolor de la Emigración Latinoamericana
groups.description:
Tejiendo identidad: Integrando nuestras raíces en comunidad.
Al dejar nuestros países de origen, ya sea por necesidad o en busca de nuevas oportunidades, nuestro sentido de identidad se desarraiga y da lugar a una identidad que “no es de aquí ni de allá”. Como resultado, el sentido de pertenencia se disloca, apareciendo un vacío interior y un sentimiento de aislamiento. Al mismo tiempo, al vivir fuera de la cultura en la que crecimos, emergen patrones que antes no eran visibles. Este programa ofrece la oportunidad de trabajar las experiencias personales de forma colectiva. En comunidad, crearemos un contenedor para observar y asimilar lo que solos no podemos.

groups.name: Loss of a Child
groups.description:
A lab for Mothers Navigating Profound Loss
This lab is for women who have experienced the loss of a child. This is a profound trauma that touches every dimension of life. Many cultures lack the ability to support the depth of grief accompanying child loss. While each mother has a unique story, many of the same emotions and experiences are shared, such as isolation. We will co-create a space to grieve and to presence our current experience of the loss. We will access our ancestral heritages, and uncover our own resilience. The intention is for a community of women to form as a supportive refuge for processing and integrating our loss.

groups.name: (In)Visibility in the Jewish–Non-Jewish Field – Global
groups.facilitator: Yocheved Sidof; Nadja Lichtenhahn; Jennifer Lees
groups.description:
A Relational Inquiry into Hiding, Visibility, and the Cost of Belonging
This Lab examines Jewish collective trauma around hiding, invisibility, and forced visibility, and how these patterns are shaped by antisemitism in the Jewish–non-Jewish field. We explore how survival strategies like passing, minimizing difference, or staying quiet become embodied over generations, and how the non-Jewish gaze—often shaped by inherited narratives that flatten or objectify—carries impact and historic weight. Our aim is to foster mutual witnessing and gently soften these patterns through slow, titrated relational presence.

groups.name: Ethics of Animal Harm: Wounds in the Collective Field
groups.facilitator: Christine Gerike; Michael Grünwald; Gabriela Zagula; Nana Gravesen
groups.description:
Opening ourselves to Animal Welfare & Ethical Violation in Factory Farming
This lab aims to bring awareness to the trauma of farm animals (chicken, cattle, pigs) on factory farms. Factory farming is a global industry that has expanded over the last century through technology and medical progress, raising billions of animals in traumatizing conditions. Animals endure confinement, overcrowding, and painful procedures, leading to stress, injury, and disease. Animals are part of our inter-being with nature. Our intention is to presence how ethical violations of animal welfare in this industry affect our collective well-being. What do we turn away from?

groups.name: The Voiceless Child Lab – Global
groups.facilitator: Diana Frank; Marg Tobias; Analisa Baker Perusse; Jacqueline Hill
groups.description:
The Collective Dimension of Losing our Voice
We will explore how voice is suppressed by collective, ancestral and individual trauma; how early experiences of silencing in the family system shape our inner world, our relationships and our place in community. Imagine a child who was not seen and heard, and learned early on that speaking up brings anger, disconnection, and/or violence. Over time, our voices fold inward to be held in the body - an ache in the chest, a loneliness inside. The authentic self retreats into the shadows. We will explore our lost voices by witnessing the space between what was never said and is now ready to emerge.

groups.name: Schweiz: Kollektive Trauma-Prägungen rund ums Geld
groups.description:
Eine Reise zu den Spannungen und Polarisierungen dieser Beziehung
In diesem Lab erforschen wir als Gruppe die Beziehungen und Prägungen der Schweiz zu Geld. Wie bildet sich die Beziehung in uns ab? Wie lebt unsere gemeinsame Vergangenheit darin? Wie zeigen sich Zeiten der Armut und des Reichtums? Welche Spannungen und Polarisierungen sind darin verborgen? Wir schaffen einen Raum, in dem wir als Gruppe in diese komplexe Beziehung hineinfühlen, und wo wir den Verletzungen und Überschreitungen gemeinsam begegnen möchten. Durch die gefühlten Begegnungen kann Heilung und Integration von Wunden entstehen, so dass sich in uns die Beziehung zu Geld wandeln darf.

groups.name: Mixed-Race Identity: In-Between Worlds & Wounds
groups.description:
Holding the tension of victim and perpetrator in our bodies and lineages
As calls for healing racialized trauma are growing, the process can become polarized into a split between people of color and white people. Yet many of us hold the tension between these polarized racial identities and/or ancestral lineages within our own bodies and psyches. This lab is for those who feel called to explore what is needed to hold this tension within ourselves—between victim and perpetrator, between racial identities, and between our ancestral lineages—so that we can ultimately become more whole.

groups.name: Lebanon: A Nexus of Collective Trauma Integration
groups.facilitator: Frank Behrens; Flavia Valgiusti; Spozhmay Orlya
groups.description:
Collective trauma plays out in governance, societal structures and families
Moving from Trauma-Inducing to Trauma-Informed to Trauma-Integrating Cultures. We turn towards realising, recognising and acknowledging the specific expression of ancestral and collective fields of trauma in Lebanon. In this Lab, we begin by forming coherence and resourcing the group, before we turn towards the specific area of trauma that we are focussing on. We address trauma fields identified with the group, e.g. anxiety of Lebanese and in the Lebanese society. Each journey has its own quality and rhythm, which we need to attune and adapt to, thus shaping a unique learning experience.

groups.name: Religiöse Traumatisierung und Seelenkraft
groups.description:
Eine Heilungsreise für Frauen in ihre authentische Spiritualität
In this LAB we researched the collective trauma of religious traumatization and how our soul power is affected by this energy as well as tackling the aspect of the collective healing journey, increasingly getting in touch with our authentic spirituality.
We were guided by the six stages of the Collective Trauma Integration Process (CTIP) by Thomas Hübl (see below).
We explored the following questions:
How is every woman individually guided by her soul?
How does your own authentic spirituality want to unfold?
How is the process of getting aware of the obstacles which do arise when we try to follow our individual felt soulpower?
What is happening when we pay attention to what is arising and was absent in this process before?
How do we bring the process of our own inner absence in relation to religious traumatization into our awareness and address these obstacles?
Where do we find ourselves in religious conditioning and trauma structures as part of our "normal" culture?
And how can our individual spiritual practice become a resource for the development of our society for a healthy, meaningful collective future?
How did we cut ourselves off from female spiritual wisdom?
What kind of phenomena arises if we tune into our soul journey as well as into our religious history and experiences as a collective?
How can we enter and stay with the discomfort?
How can we find a balance of resourcing and still tackling the theme?

groups.name: Transcending Societal Expectations for Women
groups.description:
Coming home to our Bodies as we Include & Transcend Societal Expectations
Our relationship to ourselves and how it is impacted by many internalized constructs and cultural beliefs: the messages received early in our family and environment, norms promoted on body aesthetics, the anti-aging culture and pressure to look young, the expectation to get married and have children, the expectations on women in business, amongst others. We went on a journey together to explore and unpack some of these constructs while doing embodiment practices as a way to land fully in and listen to the wisdom of our bodies. We built resources to support this embodiment journey.

groups.name: Becoming a Bridge in a Polarized World
groups.facilitator: Odile Del Giudice; Andrea Livingston; Thomas Stelling
groups.description:
Learning to Host & Integrate Trauma of Polarization within Ourselves
How do we take responsibility and find a healthy relation to stark polarization? We invited those who felt called to be the bridge in the midst of fragmentation. Our global communities have been increasingly under the pressure of highly polarized dynamics. We recognize it in wars around the world, extremism in politics, clash of religious groups, increasing racial tension, divergent approaches to the pandemic, contrasting views on climate change, and so on. Together, we examined the process of gently transforming our inner polarized parts, relating to that in our communities, and beginning to impact our collective fields of influence.

groups.name: Healing German & Jewish Wounds – Global
groups.description:
Emotional Exploration of Personal, Ancestral & Collective Wounding
We came together in solidarity to hold a healing space for one another. This was not an intellectual exploration, but rather an experiential process. We strongly recommended that those interested in the lab have a commitment to some form of daily embodiment practice, and that they be familiar with expressing their emotions in a non-violent way toward others.

groups.name: Collective Trauma in our Personal Career Paths & Work Experiences
groups.description:
Investigating our Personal Career Path
We explored all areas of collective trauma the group participants and us have encountered in our professional lives. It ranged from Patriarchy, Power Systems, and Discrimination to Mental Health.

groups.name: The Inner & Outer Work of Regeneration
groups.facilitator: Susan Belchamber; Christine Gerike; Renée Soule
groups.description:
Presencing the Hidden Trauma of Progress upon our Systems and Soil
In this lab, we explored the dramatic gains and losses throughout human history, both in our inner and outer landscapes. As we face increasing anxiety, fear, and declining well-being amid eco-trauma and climate events, we focused on slowing down to sense our grief around ecosystem decline. This process aimed to transmute suffering into fertile soil, fostering discernment around ‘progress’ and identifying potential trauma-informed regeneration actions.

groups.name: Relational Activism
groups.facilitator: Joana Breidenbach; Anjet Sekkat; Bettina Rollow
groups.description:
From Entanglement to Presencing and Beyond. How does real change happen?
Participants explored their personal relations with their activist work and reflected on the influence of collective trauma structures.

groups.name: Collective & Intergenerational Trauma in Lebanon
groups.facilitator: Frank Behrens; Spozhmay Oriya; Rawan Albina; Flavia Valgiusti
groups.description:
Exploring Effects of Trans-generational & Collective Trauma in Lebanon
In this lab, we explored the historical background of collective trauma and resilience in Lebanon, how collective and trans-generational trauma influences the construction of identity and the process of ‘othering’ as well as the development of cultural architecture, how our use of language reflects and reinforces the contemporary effects of these traumas, how collective and trans-generational traumas manifest themselves in times of crisis (e.g. economic crisis, Covid-19, climate crises) and the possibility of coherent we-spaces and the process of witnessing collective and trans-generational trauma leading to integration.

groups.name: Unlearning Patriarchy to Embrace Fluid Leadership
groups.facilitator: Jana Schmitz; Leo Meyer-Schwickerath; Silke Breithaupt
groups.description:
Exploring the Patriarchal Impact on our Leadership Experience
The lab highlights patriarchy’s essence as a power-over dominance for nearly 20,000 years, shaping leadership styles and posing challenges in the modern landscape. The past century’s rapid changes demand heightened response-ability in leadership, creating tension between current needs and historical imprints. The lab serves as a space to digest and integrate this inner tension, offering participants insight into the profound impact of patriarchy on organizational leadership dynamics and our relationship to leading and following. It facilitates understanding and adaptation to the evolving demands of leadership and therefore of our inner structures in the face of environmental shifts.

groups.name: Trauma in the Healthcare System
groups.facilitator: Gabriela Zagula; Michael Gruenwald; Beate Küchle
groups.description:
Exploring Fragmentation and Dysfunction & Inviting Health and Healing
We explored layers in the health care system (HCS) that are mute, frozen, unseen, or excluded to become more aware and conscious of their effects. These effects may be hindering the development of the HCS to a level where there is abundance and safety in the system, where life and healing are at the center.

groups.name: A Cut from Art
groups.facilitator: Jennifer Krier; Isaac Shamah; Catharine Anderson
groups.description:
Collective Trauma & Creative Loss
We explored layers of undigested trauma around creativity. The Lab provided a context to collectively presence and relate to the larger forces impacting our creativity. We looked at the ways survival mechanisms impeded our artistic activation and the ways that post-traumatic resilience can be a resource of the creative process.

groups.name: Exploring Loneliness
groups.facilitator: Miriam Nelken; Emma Philbin Bowman; Tacha Lawrie
groups.description:
Presencing our Personal, Cultural, Ancestral & Collective Experiences of Loneliness
In our “Exploring Loneliness” lab, we explored many aspects of loneliness, focusing on the personal, ancestral, and collective aspects. We inquired into a range of themes, including how our early history informed our current experiences of loneliness; the ways in which each of us co-creates our experiences of loneliness, how this might serve us; the forms of loneliness we learned in our families of origin and cultural environments. We also presenced some collective aspects of loneliness. Throughout the process, we cultivated a quality of receptive presence and the possibility to lean on this as a primary resource in our journey.

groups.name: Victim – Perpetrator Dynamics Through the Individual, Generational & Collective Lens
groups.facilitator: Michal Gaia Golan; Alanda Becker; Lysan Boshuyzen
groups.description:
What Holds the Past Alive in Us Today? How Do We Ease and Release the Entanglement?
Transgression binds victims and perpetrators together and the entanglement may impact our sense of safety, identity, freedom and belonging. What is the residual impact of victimisation and perpetration upon our emotional, mental and physical being? How does ancestral V-P dynamics continue to impact future generations? And, what steps can we take as individuals and communities, to reconcile trauma that might hold us in a state of stasis/reaction? This lab explored what it takes to shed light on the entangled past alive in us today, then taking initial steps forward with a coherent and compassionate response.

groups.name: Aufarbeitung der Corona-Zeit
groups.description:
Das Ungesagte, Ungehörte, Ungefühlte und Unverstandene darf auftauchen
Die Corona-Zeit hat Spuren in unserem Leben hinterlassen, im gesellschaftlichen wie im inneren. Die extreme Polarisierung schien damals unüberbrückbar - wohl auch deswegen, weil sie in vielen Menschen starke Angst hervorgerufen hat - und in unsicheren Zeiten beziehen wir gerne feste Positionen, weil sie sich sicherer anfühlen. Gleich mehrere "alte Ängste" waren aufgerufen - die Angst vor Krankheit und Tod, die Angst, an jemand anderes Krankheit schuld zu sein, aber auch die Angst, seine wirtschaftliche Existenz zu verlieren oder in den demokratischen Grundrechten eingeschränkt zu werden. Mit diesen und ähnlichen Themen wird uns die Aufarbeitung konfrontieren.

groups.name: An Inner Exploration of ‘The South’
groups.facilitator: Hannah Sadtler; Kelly Chambers; Clayton McClintock
groups.description:
History, Identity, Trauma & Resource in the Southern United States
The history and culture of the Southern United States are inextricably linked to that of the US as a whole. We endeavored to explore our relationships – individually and collectively – with the complex archeology of trauma and resilience, othering and belonging in this region. Through a deeper sensing of how the South lives in each of us, our intention was to support the healing of the multi-layered collective traumas centered in “The South” and offer something unifying to the collective field.

groups.name: The Global Legacy of the Great Famine in Ireland
groups.facilitator: Bill McCart; Simon Courtney; Kathy Scott
groups.description:
Healing the Wounds of An Gorta Mór & Exploring What it Means to be Irish
Our lab explored the legacy of the Great Famine (1845-52), in which more than 1 million Irish died. More than 1 million emigrated during this time, and there were successive waves of emigration that created an Irish diaspora that today numbers more than 44 million. The lab is not so much about the history but about people’s experience of that history. What did the Irish have to do to survive the Famine? How does the Famine echo into our lives in the present? How is the legacy of the famine different for those who left and those who remained?

groups.name: Spiritual Trauma & Our Personal Path to the Divine
groups.facilitator: Susanne Breit; Katherine Poco-Enders; Brigitte Kotzke
groups.description:
Journey through the 4 Pillars of Trauma Integration
This lab offered a space to explore spiritual trauma - experiences of disconnection, shame, or isolation in relation to the Sacred due to familial, religious, or cultural conditioning. Through self-regulation, meditation, shadow work, and contemplation (the four pillars), we created an emergent field for deep healing, post-traumatic growth, and the integration of individual, ancestral, and collective trauma.

groups.name: Wrestling with Jewish Belonging
groups.description:
Relating to Our Jewish Heritage & Spiritual Roots in Challenging Times
In this Lab, we explored our Jewish spiritual roots and how we experience this connection in the present moment. We reflected on how being Jewish during this period of world history affects our sense of inner security, grounding, and spiritual connection. We also examined how collective, ancestral, and individual trauma shapes these experiences.

groups.name: Collective Trauma – Organization & its Stakeholders
groups.facilitator: Reinier Tilanus; Angela von Rotz; Mathias Holzmann
groups.description:
Diving Deep into the Unconscious Patterns that Define an Organization
We set out to explore collective trauma patterns within an organisation or company to understand how the collective dimension of trauma manifests within the day- to-day operations of an organization and as a consequence impacts the fabric of our economy.

groups.name: Collective Trauma & Resilience – Findhorn Community
groups.description:
Healing our Future - Creating Purpose Through Healing our Relating
We invited participants to join us on a journey of refining our inner listening and our capacity to host and integrate diverse ideas with equanimity, in order to allow healing and innovative movements. We aimed to shed light on: • The loss of connection to ourselves, our community, nature, and the wider world • The loss of a common vision • What's needed to sustain or return to alignment with our core values • The individual and interpersonal conflicts underlying polarisation • Unconscious or unspoken assumptions and agreements • Confusion between spiritual and regressive states

groups.name: Pathways to a Decolonized Future
groups.facilitator: Shayla Wright; Jo Hardy; Rita Maria Brown
groups.description:
Exploring the Ongoing Impact of Colonization & How We Can Begin to Heal It
We explored the individual, ancestral and collective imprints of colonization on the mind, body, heart and nervous system. One aspect of this was supporting each participant to research and learn about their own “trauma mountain,” the trauma history related to colonization from their own culture. This opened up a space to feel and sense more deeply how colonization lives and moves in us, from moment to moment. We also opened up different spaces to discover what decolonization might look or feel like, through movement, dialogue, reflection and art. Decolonization is a vast and complex topic; each participant was free to follow the aspects and themes that were alive and relevant for them. Colonization and decolonization of the body was one aspect that was very powerful and quite challenging for many participants.

groups.name: ‘Climate Crisis’ Lab
groups.description:
Embedding ourselves in Embodiment, Earth and Emerging Future
We explored how our disconnect from ourselves, each other and the Earth gives birth to the great crises of our times, including the Climate Crisis. And how we can bring deep curiosity, compassion and love to these places of disconnect. We touched on the trauma that leads us to disconnect and the trauma that grows from our disconnect. We explored how to connect more deeply to Earth and how to re-learn the language of Earth.

groups.name: Trauma in Education Lab
groups.facilitator: Silke Weiss; Kathrin Loewe; Dana Revnic
groups.description:
Exploring & Healing Wounds and Scars from Educational Past and Present
In this lab, we explored together how collective trauma affects the way we raise our children, at home and in school systems. In the first layer, we became aware of trauma from our own experience as well as cultural and collective aspects in the past throughout education that are still alive in us. In the second layer, we tuned into the current sources of traumatization in actual school and family environments, including actual reports of child diseases and dangers through social media. We invited other relevant topics coming from group interest.

groups.name: Mitigating Trauma in Your Organization
groups.description:
Invitation for Organizational Leaders
Recognizing and mitigating trauma is a core leadership challenge. Leaders are becoming more aware of the impact of individual and collective trauma on the health of employees and the overall organization. Unaddressed trauma has been shown to prohibit organizations from being innovative and able to realize visionary futures. In this cutting-edge exploration, a small group of organizational executives grew their understanding of what trauma is and how it shows up, exploring ways to mediate and proactively address the presence of trauma in their organizations, and personally grow as instruments of restoration.

groups.name: Kollektives Trauma & Patriarchat
groups.facilitator: Luna Garcia Fernandez; Julia Bulik; Sina Gruber
groups.description:
Wo kommen wir her? Wo sind wir? Wo wollen wir hin?
We dedicate ourselves to topics such as body image, care work, relationship dynamics, masculinity/femininity expectations, and sexism. We explore the emotional and psychological structures within us: How does the collective trauma of patriarchy manifest in our bodies, thoughts, and emotions? What contradictions do we feel within ourselves regarding patriarchal structures? Which things do we want to feel or talk about openly, and which do we prefer to avoid? How does patriarchy live within us, and how can we heal from it—not just theoretically, but also on a nervous system level? What does a safe space for healing look like?
Our focus is on emotional process work. To support this, we use small and large group work, lectures, discussions, and meditations.

groups.name: Men, Fathers, Gods – Trauma & Alignment in Men’s Lineages
groups.facilitator: Stefan Beier; Martin Bruders; Robert Buxbaum
groups.description:
The International Men’s Lab
The Men’s Lab explored trauma in men’s lineages and the collective – the role of fatherhood in it, and our alignment with God. Creative and destructive forces struggle in us. We have inherited our forefathers’ wounds and inner strength, their fighting, and their care. Together we dived into the roots of our manhood, and their expression in our lives. We explored the divine dimension: our way of bowing down, of leading and being led, and the relation between courage and grace. The qualities of fatherhood we find in God – in what we trust.

groups.name: Being Jewish: Persecution and Perpetration
groups.facilitator: Robin Alfred; Teddy Frank; Anna Mollitor
groups.description:
Persecution & Perpetration
The collective trauma of being Jewish - both the experience of being persecuted and that of being perpetrators. We explored the complexity and uncomfortable reality of how oppression lives in us through being both victims and perpetrators, and the relationship between the two. We approached these themes from contemporary, historical and ancestral dimensions, tapping into the collective experience of Being Jewish.

groups.name: Kollektives Trauma in Journalismus & Medien
groups.facilitator: Silke Liniewski; Jessica Hauk; Peter Ryser
groups.description:
Wie können wir Nachrichten bewusst gestalten, konsumieren und verdauen?
Journalismus und Medien sind eine Herausforderung - sowohl für die Menschen, die sie aufbereiten und machen, als auch für alle Nutzenden. Viele Menschen konsumieren Medien entweder zu viel oder lehnen sie ganz ab. Wie können Mediengestalter:innen und Nachrichtenmacher:innen Informationen traumainformiert aufbereiten? Und wie können Nutzende für sich selbst einen guten und gesunden Ansatz bei der Mediennutzung finden? Wie können wir von der Polarisierung zu einem gesunden Verhalten und einer angemessenen Haltung gegenüber Journalismus und Medien kommen? In unserem Lab haben wir uns mit kollektiven Traumata im Journalismus und in den Medien befasst und das Potenzial von traumainformiertem Journalismus und traumaintegrierter Mediennutzung untersucht.

groups.name: Habitando el cuerpo femenino
groups.facilitator: Stephanie Pizarro; Maria Soledad Troya; Karla Mejia
groups.description:
Un viaje colectivo de autodescubrimiento, a través del cuerpo femenino - Latam
The lab focused on exploring trauma symptoms in women, emphasizing disconnection, violence, and societal challenges. Through shared experiences, participants fostered a collective consciousness, enabling healing and integration of collective trauma. They drew on cultural resources and ancestral resilience inherent in Latin American femininity.
- We reflected on the symptoms of trauma in women today, and their effects on our disconnection, rejection, violence and criticism towards our bodies.
- We explored our fragmentation and dissociation in relation to our self-contact.
- We created a field of connection and shared consciousness, where we could feel, transform, heal and integrate parts of the collective trauma.
- We connected with our being, becoming and belonging as women, in the face of the current challenges of our society.
- We recognized the wealth of resources we have as women connected to Latin America, including our cultural collective intelligence and ancestral resilience.
Our intentions were to attract more light and manifest it, practice abundance, and love, connect with the feminine, include polarity in the body, make teachings tangible, and create a healing path for women.

groups.name: Finding our Way Home
groups.facilitator: Ingrid Pickel; Wendy Buffett; Eve-Marie Elkin
groups.description:
Cultivating our Capacity to Sense a Place
Our lab investigated the intersection between our body-mind-system and the land we are born in, live in or are drawn to. How does being in a heartfelt resonance with the land inform us? When listening to the land, what do we learn about our individual, ancestral, and collective history? Can we feel the interconnectedness of all beings and our interwovenness in the fabric of a place? We explored belonging as a key component of a sense of home.

groups.name: Collective & Transgenerational Trauma in the Balkans Lab II
groups.facilitator: Susanne Stillhammer; Marc Padberg; Nikola Jurisic
groups.description:
Exploring the Unintegrated Past & Inviting Healing in the Present
Our written and shared intention was to create a safe space for all present to share and witness each other’s beauty and pain and through that support the healing and integration of traumatizing experiences in them and their ancestors, in service of creating a lighter, more inclusive and integrated life in the region and beyond.
We explored the effects of the Yugoslav wars of the 1990s on the individual and ancestral level. When exploring ancestral trauma, we touched upon the historic roots of the 1990s war, in particular the events in the Balkans during the second World War. In the exploration, participants representing the different former combatting ethno-religious groups shared, processed their painful experiences and discovered the commonalities in these. When meeting in-person, we deepened our exploration through the connection with the physical land in Visoko, Bosnia-Herzegovina. We experienced a retreat with intensity and depth in which we also shared dance, singing and meals.

groups.name: Healing the Masculine & Feminine with the Earth
groups.facilitator: Louise Marra; Patrick Dougherty; Carolin Thywissen
groups.description:
Restoring our Connection to the Earth to Heal Ourselves & the Web of Life
This lab focused on exploring the disconnection of both the masculine and the feminine from the earth and each other and building the capacities and processes needed for re-connection. It involved a range of online sessions, solo 4-6 hour quests in nature, creative expression, and gender-focused sessions. We sought an intimate, committed group to explore the nature of a connected and disconnected masculine and feminine. We experimented with deep processes to restore the web of life by healing and reconnecting the traumatized masculine and feminine to the earth and each other.
